feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: clear positioning, relevant scope, and good evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused metrics in recent roles.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong headline and consistent progression from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is polished and professional overall, with strong domain alignment in digital governance, Drupal, analytics, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would sharpen structure and save space for achievements.  
- Add more measurable outcomes, especially in the freelance role and project section: quantify improvements in traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” is preferable to “organization wide”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (some bullets use serial commas, some do not); “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “English (native), French (A2, learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats language already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”
- Add a scale cue from recent experience, e.g. “including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel noun/verb structure for smoother style: “Specializes in enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- Consider aligning “AI-enabled user experiences” with the rest of the CV by using “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities closely mirrors Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise phrasing and reduce “operations/infrastructure/systems” repetition.
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial workflows • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- If space is tight, shorten further by dropping “public-sector” or “multimedia” depending on target role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics,” and “multimedia” are already emphasized in the header, Topline Skills, and recent experience.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” overlaps with both the summary and “Editorial systems and governance” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and purpose.
- Use parallel, outcome-oriented phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and trim stacked descriptors.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.
- Consider this rewrite:  
  • **AI Hybrid Search** — Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  • **We Are Counties Microsite** — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a scalable modular architecture.  
  • **Organization Anniversary Campaign** — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display integrated with the main site.  
  • **Advocacy Video Series** — Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video work are already reflected in recent roles; keep this section shorter and more project-specific to avoid repetition.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale where possible to distinguish it from the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications operations improvement for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led line: “Built cross-functional content, analytics, and publishing workflows to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more concise and outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, process time reduced, search relevance gains, or engagement/conversion improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo governance language; keep this version focused on what changed or improved.
- AI-enabled search also appears in Recent Projects/footer; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets added outcomes rather than broad reach statements.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a high-volume public-sector organization.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen channel bullet with performance if available: include email open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, or campaign results; otherwise shorten to avoid generic scale language.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while establishing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video studio/buildout overlaps with older NACo roles’ video production; keep this focused on “built first in-house studio” and move recurring programming details to earlier entries.
- Governance/editorial coordination repeats themes in the 2018–2022 role; emphasize enterprise-level ownership here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope growth, team coordination, and channel ownership at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show level and remit: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Combine newsletter impact into one sharper bullet: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Strengthen operations language with clearer ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video work also appears in the 2015–2018 role and footer project list; avoid repeating “weekly video updates” phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent role bullets. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and higher-value strategic themes rather than repeating generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale instead of broad terms here (e.g., enterprise web, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than in this skills list.
- Keep phrasing parallel: noun-based, 3–5 words each, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with recent experience in campaign/storytelling and editorial coordination; keep only if other skills are trimmed.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of listing platforms flatly.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search, front-end implementation.
- Remove lower-signal or dated items here (“jQuery,” possibly “WordPress” if not central to recent work); keep detailed tool inventory in Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation and Airtable-based systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full platform/tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overusing the exact phrase elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the strategic value expected in a topline skills area. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, KPI design and executive reporting”
- Group tools more tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger phrasing: “search, content and conversion performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and measurement frameworks • KPI design and executive reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and conversion performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills focused on strategic capability, not another full software list.
- Avoid overemphasizing SEO unless it is a meaningful part of recent roles.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Video editing and post-production • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better reflect the in-house studio build.

- Keep only 4–5 items; remove lower-signal phrasing like “Studio operations” unless you can make it more specific (“Studio buildout and operations”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- This section overlaps with NACo bullets about studio buildout, livestreams, and video programming, so avoid repeating identical language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal level of expertise and emphasize the most relevant platform: Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If accurate, add proficiency cues: **Drupal (expert) • WordPress (advanced) • SharePoint/Power Pages (working knowledge) • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially relevant to recent roles; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep ordering by relevance/recency, with Drupal first and Microsoft ecosystem tools grouped together.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**. Consider keeping the detailed version in one place and shortening the other.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere; don’t repeat that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more senior and implementation-focused by emphasizing modern tools and how you apply them.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at this level.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if still actively used in recent work; otherwise de-emphasize it as older tech.
- If space allows, add light context: “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations.”
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep it here only if you want to signal CI/CD specifically.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by purpose for faster scanning: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking)
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first; drop any rarely used platform rather than listing every PM tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they materially support your systems/operations positioning

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare to show level of ownership or relevance. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize systems expertise rather than repeat channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten content to: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief: Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, and member engagement systems
- If space allows, prioritize by strongest/recent use first; e.g., Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or audience-size claims here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations,” so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills.” It should emphasize analysis/optimization capabilities and use tighter, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design & leadership reporting • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI design & leadership reporting” to sound more strategic and outcome-oriented.
- Use “Experimentation (A/B testing)” instead of just “A/B testing” to signal broader optimization capability.
- Order tools by depth/importance, with GA4/BigQuery/BI first to align with recent NACo analytics infrastructure work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly mirrors “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this section more tool-focused while keeping the other more capability-focused.
- If space is tight, drop either “Looker Studio” or “Power BI” only if one was clearly secondary in practice.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since strategy/leadership are already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer management phrase only if accurate: “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with later governance/operations bullets; keep this at a tactical level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry lighter than later roles since your stronger digital leadership story appears from 2015 onward.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media entries; keep this focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since management progression is better shown in later NACo roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed skills/category list than a sharp technical tools entry. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to software/tools only or clearly separate tools from capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production workflows”
